title: No matched US bird survey had both a start at 25 C or more and PM2.5 above 35 ug/m3 in 2006-2024
abstract: We tested whether warm survey starts change the link between same-day PM2.5 and recorded bird taxa. We used the fixed 2025 Breeding Bird Survey release and EPA daily data for 2006-2024. Each route used one site within 50 km, with records in both study periods. This rule gave 2,715 matched runs on 241 routes. None had both a start at 25 C or more and PM2.5 above 35 ug/m3. These are coverage benchmarks, not biological thresholds. Four region-period models used 2,109 runs, route-observer effects, state-year effects, weather, date, and survey time. All four warmth-pollution interaction intervals included zero. The early West model had only 12 residual degrees of freedom. Separate future-exposure and control checks did not give a clear interaction. One western distance check was not identified. The results do not show that joint extremes are harmless. Accepted-run selection, sparse monitor coverage, daily exposure timing, and uncertain detection limit inference. The package contains a fixed-site panel, daily site data, source hashes, code, figures, and an offline reproduction check.

display.caption: The 2,109 primary runs have no joint record above the two coverage benchmarks. The wider 2,715-run matched sample also has none. The benchmarks are a start at 25 C or more and same-day PM2.5 above 35 ug/m3. They are not biological thresholds.

Fixed-effect estimates. Left: PM2.5 slope at a 15 C start, with individual 95% intervals. Right: change in that slope per 10 C warmer start, with four-test intervals. Units are 100 times log-taxon change per 10 ug/m3. Wide western intervals show poor precision.

Interaction checks use individual 95% intervals. Future exposure is measured seven days after the survey. Same-day and future models use common rows before the repeated-group rule. One early West 25 km check is not identified.
